title: The Secret Pages of Leonardo
paragraphs: Leonardo da Vinci is famous for paintings like the Mona Lisa. But he was also a careful thinker who wanted to understand everything around him. He wrote his ideas in notebooks, and thousands of these pages still exist today.

The notebooks are full of drawings and notes. Leonardo drew the bones and muscles of the human body. He watched birds closely and drew machines that he hoped could help people fly. He also studied water, plants, rocks and light.

One unusual thing about the notebooks is his handwriting. Leonardo often wrote from right to left, with the letters turned backwards. To read it easily, you need to hold the page up to a mirror. Nobody knows for sure why he did this. Some experts think it was simply easier for him, because he used his left hand.

sources.claim: Leonardo da Vinci Mona Lisa gibi tablolarıyla ünlüdür; fikirlerini defterlere yazdı ve binlerce sayfası günümüze ulaştı.
Defterlerde insan anatomisi, kuşların uçuşu ve uçan makineler, su, bitkiler, kayalar ve ışık üzerine çizim ve notlar vardır.
Leonardo'nun anatomi çizimlerinin önemli bir bölümü Royal Collection'dadır.
sources.source: Royal Collection Trust (Leonardo da Vinci drawings collection); https://www.rct.uk/

sources.claim: Leonardo çoğunlukla sağdan sola ayna yazısıyla yazdı; solak olduğu bir açıklama olarak öne sürülür, kesin neden bilinmez.
